Governor rules

Three HARD checks plus the closed-allowlist check, all permanent and un-overridable by any human approval. fired counts and the detail strings are from this run; the descriptions are fixed-behaviour documentation read off venueadminops.governor.

RuleWhat it checksfiredExample detail (verbatim from the governor)
:effect-not-proposeEvery proposal's :effect must be :propose. Any other value is, by construction, a claim to actuate outside governance.1HARD · :effect は :propose のみ許可されるが :commit が提案された
:op-not-allowedThe op is outside the governor's closed allowlist. Also how a phase gate surfaces: an op the current phase does not enable degrades to :noop, which is not on the allowlist.2HARD · :noop は許可された操作(closed allowlist)に含まれない
:scope-excludedThe proposal's op/summary/rationale/cites/value are flattened into one blob and scanned for artistic, casting, programming/curatorial, pricing or safety-authority territory. Permanent — this actor's charter excludes that territory structurally.4HARD · 創作/キャスティング/キュレーション/料金設定/安全当局の判断領域に触れる提案は永久に禁止
:venue-unverifiedThe target venue must exist in the store AND be independently :registered? and :verified? there. Re-derived from the venue's own record — a proposal's claim about its venue is never trusted.2HARD · venue-3 は未登録または未検証の会場 -- いかなる提案も進められない

Scope scan dictionary: 32 case-insensitive terms from governor/scope-excluded-terms — artistic, artistic direction, casting, complaint, compliance enforcement, compliance-enforcement, creative decision, creative-decision, curatorial, investigat, license, pricing, programming, revenue, safety authority, safety enforcement, safety-authority, talent, talent selection, ticket price, キャスティング, キュレーション, チケット価格, プログラミング, 出演者選, 創作, 創作判断, 創造的, 売上, 料金, 通報, 違反.

SOFT escalation gates: op ∈ governor/always-escalate-ops (:flag-safety-concern) or confidence < governor/confidence-floor = 0.6.

What the SSoT actually retains

Measured, not assumed: the key column is the union of the keys present on the records the store really kept this run.

KeyRetained?Notes
:decisionretainedrendered
:operation-idretainedpresent, NOT rendered — a random UUID, would break byte-identical reruns
:proposalretainedrendered (op, summary, rationale, cites, effect, value)
:timestampretainedpresent, NOT rendered — wall clock, would break byte-identical reruns
:venue-idretainedrendered in every table
:contextdroppedthe operator context {:actor-id "venue-admin-1", :actor-role :venue-operations-coordinator} is passed into run-operation on every scenario and is not copied into either the committed record or the ledger fact
:governor-resultdroppedHARD violations are not written to the ledger; the ledger table above joins them from the live run state (audit only; not retained in record)

Measured at render time, not assumed: scanning every committed record and every ledger fact this run produced, none of :actor-id, :approval, :approved-by, :approver, :by, :context, :operator, :reviewed-by is present. Two separate reasons, and it matters which:

  • Nobody could have approved. This actor has no approval or resume seam at all — operation/hold and operation/escalate are terminal states. Held and escalated proposals in the tables above are waiting on a human who has no way, in this codebase, to answer. So the missing approver is not a lost field: no approval event ever happened.
  • The operator who proposed IS dropped. The build-time driver passes {:actor-id "venue-admin-1", :actor-role :venue-operations-coordinator} as context into every run-operation call, and operation/commit, operation/hold and operation/escalate all build their record from :operation-id :timestamp :venue-id :proposal :decision only. The proposing operator's identity is therefore absent from the SSoT — (driver input; not retained in record). The store's own docstring promises “approved by whom is always a query over an immutable log”; as of this build that promise is not kept by the record shape.

Regenerate: kbb -M:dev:render-html [out-file]. Deterministic — byte-identical across reruns against the same seed. :operation-id (random UUID) and :timestamp (wall clock) are deliberately withheld from the page rather than silently dropped; see the retention table.

Pipeline note: operation/run-operation is a plain -> threading pipeline, not a langgraph.graph/state-graph — this repo has no langgraph dependency, so there is no interrupt-before resume seam and a hold is terminal. README.md still describes a StateGraph; operation.cljc's own docstring records the drift.
